title: Leadership Traits
paragraphs: Having discussed the features of land and time and the modes of love behaviour, it is now necessary to explain the distinctive regional features of the five tracts of land (karupporuḷ).

The deity worshipped, food for the stomach, animals, trees, plants, creepers, birds, leather instruments, occupation, the lyre and other string instruments and things of these sorts would come under karupporuḷ. Place, water, flower, etc., would also come under karupporuḷ.

> God, food, animal, tree, > Bird, drum, occupation and the lute > And such of these > Constitute the distinctive physical features of the given tract of land. > > (Poruḷatikāram : Akattiṇai iyal, verse 18)
Though, in this list of karupporuḷ, flowers and birds are allotted to specific divisions of land, they might be shown to belong to other divisions of land.

> Where the flora and fauna occur > Not marked proper to the land and season in question though, > They be deemed > Characteristic of that land and that season. > > (Poruḷatikāram : Akattiṇai iyal, verses 19)
Just as mullai land is inhabited by shepherds and hunters, the other types of land also have farmers, etc. engaged in occupations characteristic of those geographical divisions:

> Cowherds and huntsmen > Designate region-specific persons of the masculine gender; > There are other names of principal characters such as these two > Drawn that they are on the region’s occupation.

> We find on reflection that > Inhabitants of other regions too > Have their names derived from the mores of their region > And from the occupation of that region. > > (Poruḷatikāram : Akattiṇai iyal, verses 21, 22)
> Such representation of kaikkiḷai and peruntiṇai > Does mark men of other menial occupations too. > > (Poruḷatikāram : Akattiṇai iyal, verse 24)
Tolkāppiyar does not go by the social status, and assigns the position of the hero and heroine even to those folks engaged in lowly occupations.
There are, however, some scholars amongst us who tend to misinterpret ēval marapu (menial work) as that of ordering others.
